 By Letters to the editor | insight@orlandosentinel.com PUBLISHED: November 21, 2026 at 5:30 AM EST Getting your Trinity Audio player ready... Jolly earned a place at the table
 Democratic gubernatorial candidate David Jolly won peninsular Florida by 26,685 votes, flipping seven counties, despite a huge GOP registration advantage. It took the fire-engine red West Panhandle for Byron Donalds to eke out his win — hardly carte blanche to push the cruel, myopic policies and cronyism that brand Ron DeSantis. More non-Panhandle citizens wanted Jolly. Bear hunts, data centers, ecocide-by-bulldozer and meddling in personal health decisions remain starkly unpopular.
 “The voters have spoken!” begs nuance since the GOP lost so much credibility hitching itself to Donald Trump. That Jolly retook Miami-Dade, Palm Beach and Hillsborough counties should stun our president, now surrounded by a sapphire-blue majority. One wonders if his psyche can grip the nation’s loud rebuke of his presidency.
 Winter Park went strongly for Jolly. Angie Nixon’s “Democratic socialist” label may have sparked split votes here, but both candidates gave notice to the Republican Party that it can no longer smugly tune out the millions not sharing its agenda. Nixon drew many young people with her message. Statistically, some Republicans had to have voted for her too.
 In my view, Jolly ran an honest, inclusive campaign. To many of us, he and Gwen Graham were a rare offering; it’s sad that preposterous sums of corporate and billionaire money bought just enough misleading ads to hurt them. Post-blue tsunami, Donalds can’t ignore Jolly’s 4 million-plus voters.  If he’s smart, he will court Jolly’s input on what reforms his supporters wanted. We all share a stake in Florida’s future.
 — Rebecca Eagan, Winter Park 
 Florida Dems drop the ball
 The majority of American voters decided they wanted to be on the right side of history.
 But Florida didn’t get the memo.
 Famously home to grifters of all stripes, Florida voters opted to elect people I see as con men and crooks to lead us for four more years.
 This rogues’ gallery includes the likes of Byron Donalds, Ashley Moody and James Uthmeier. The latter two may now face no consequences for their roles in the Hope Florida scandal.
 The silver linings are that Republicans failed to win any of the four congressional districts they gerrymandered, and they no longer have a supermajority in the state House.
 And while I am thrilled with the national results, I can’t help but feel sadness for Florida.
 Democrats had a generational opportunity to flip a Senate seat and take back the governor’s mansion. Angie Nixon infused something that had been missing on the state’s left for a long time: enthusiasm. But by not providing enough support (financial and otherwise), the party establishment dropped the ball.
 So here’s an idea. Let’s make Angie Nixon chair of the Florida Democratic Party.
 — I. Scott Singerman, Delray Beach 
 A Daylight Saving Time compromise
 All this arguing and side-taking about permanent Daylight Saving Time versus permanent Standard Time is absurd. About half of the population adamantly prefers one and half the other, for their own perfectly good personal reasons. But what polls say they really despise is the changing from one to the other twice a year. The solution is simple: Create a permanent Middle Time or Compromise Time halfway between the two. That way, everyone gets some of what they like and some of what they don’t like. With no more time changes, people will eventually get used to it.
 — Herb Piper, Winter Springs
